note: Commercially he is a good fit: he runs a construction business and reasons about it like an owner ("I don't charge people the basement price because I don't want them to expect basement outcomes"), he has a discretionary spending threshold and never said he could not afford it — only that this sits above the level he decides alone — and health is squarely the neglected area rather than a crisis. Where he fails is the starting point, and he supplies the disqualifying number himself: 5'9", 240 lb, target 190, "that would be about 50 pounds to lose, which is a significant amount, I know." The stated ICP excludes exactly that — "it's not like we have dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight, who are just like, I need to just lose weight." The exclusion is not a clean fit though, and this is the interesting part: the second half of the stated criterion is "and I hate working out", and he is the opposite — a former college track and field thrower with a health and exercise science degree, a current gym membership he likes using, and kettlebells he already trains with at home. So he trips the weight half of the exclusion and clears the attitude half entirely. He is evidence that the stated ICP's single most concrete screen is measuring the wrong variable: it screens on pounds when the thing that actually predicts fit is training history and self-direction.
